records.text: A Firewing blood elf guard at Firewing Point, this Bloodwarder serves the force tied to Kael'thas and Illidan. In combat, it threatens intruders and boasts that it will take their energy and life.
A Firewing blood elf defender at Firewing Point, this guard serves the force tied to Kael'thas and Illidan. Its battle cries urge allies to stop fleeing enemies and declare loyalty to Kael'thas.
A gryphon rider serving as a guard.
A bat rider serving as a guard.

Lady Dena Kennedy is an Alliance frontier officer at Allerian Stronghold, concerned about arakkoa raids on supply lines and attacks on scouts. Because she knows little about arakkoa society, she seeks intelligence from Rilak the Redeemed, leader of a non-hostile group in Shattrath.

A Shadow Council executioner stationed at the ruined village near Auchindoun, this rank-and-file soldier's chatter mixes concern over the Council's loss of control of Murmur with ordinary complaints about pay and duty. The speakers mention joining for a chance at the academy, social plans in Shattrath, and thoughts of leaving the service; their words suggest an imperfectly committed recruit-facing company rather than a uniformly zealous force.

A Firewing blood-elf warlock serving Kael'thas's cause, this hostile combatant calls on his allegiance and threatens enemies who try to escape. Its combat speech marks it as a committed fighter at Firewing Point.
A fel-orc fighter among the Bonechewer forces threatening Stonebreaker, the Devastator attacks with a snap kick.

A Broken Skeleton is an undead remnant haunting the Bone Wastes beyond Auchindoun. The draenei spirits there are described as corrupted by Auchindoun’s explosion and left wandering in torment; this skeleton is among the creatures Soolaveen asks visitors to put to rest.
A Bonechewer Backbreaker is one of the fel orcs threatening camps in Terokkar. Local efforts focus on thinning their forces before the buildup draws reinforcements or wider attention.

This Shadow Council summoner joined after being promised academy tuition and says an uncle expects them to enroll next season. They miss the Shadow Labyrinth despite hoping the ruined village becomes a forward base, worry about the Council's loss of control over Murmur, and are considering mustering out; off-shift drinks and a leather-ball league connect them with their fellow summoners.
Wrekt Warrior is a combatant in the Hellfire Peninsula area. Its native combat behavior includes Strike and Whirlwind.
Wrekt Seer is a combatant in the Hellfire Peninsula area. Its native behavior periodically applies Lightning Shield to itself while out of combat.

Mokasa oversees work at Stonebreaker Hold and expects news from Swamprat Post, whose progress matters to her outpost. She says Alliance outriders have killed too many of her messengers, giving her a practical reason to value the report and the routes her runners travel.

Andarl is a mage and scholar at Allerian Stronghold. He has experienced spells fizzling in Terokkar and suspects nearby warp stalkers are disrupting magic. Though known as a scholar of draenei relics, he admits he has had little time to study them; he also reads an arakkoa message about preparations at Skettis and urges that Thander be told. His own work spans magical disturbances and intelligence about local ruins and arakkoa activity.
A Boulderfist ogre subordinate in the Bleeding Hollow Ruins. Kilrath’s plan calls for killing several of Unkor’s subordinates before pressuring Unkor for information; invaders are among the targets.

Unkor the Ruthless is the Boulderfist leader encountered in the Bleeding Hollow Ruins. Under pressure, he pleads for his life and explains that Warmaul has taken much of Boulderfist’s land in Nagrand and killed many of its people. He says Krol has gone missing and Lantresor of the Blade rules during Boulderfist’s turmoil.

Kilrath is a lowly rogue and scout sent by Jorin Deadeye to investigate the ogres at the Bleeding Hollow Ruins. He calls them peculiar and stupid, and says Unkor makes the lesser ogres dance. Kilrath arranges to pressure Unkor for information, then sends the account to Jorin, admitting he does not know what to do with it. He says he will hide in the bushes if needed.

Kurgatok is a warlock at Stonebreaker Hold who studies the arakkoa. When strange writing implicated the arakkoa in Dugar’s interrogation and preparations at Skettis, he translated enough to recognize a wider threat and urged that Rokag be told. He sent his imp, Keb’ezil, to investigate magical disturbances from warp stalkers; their bickering suggests a familiar, exasperated partnership.

Malukaz is an orc of Stonebreaker Hold seeking to restore his people’s bond with Terokkar’s wolf spirit. He believes the spirit was left behind when the orc clans departed, and prepares wolf-pelt vestments and an incense ceremony to call it home. Though unsure the summons will be answered, he sees the renewed bond as the beginning of his journey.

Rakoria works at Stonebreaker Hold on a commercial oil venture: she gathers Olemba seeds, presses them, and tests possible uses, arranging for Grek to try a sample on his weapon. After learning it is mana oil, she sees a market for it and orders it shipped, though Grek is an exception. She is described as sharp and capable, but follows profit and may not have the Horde’s interests at heart; she also judges progress at Swamprat Post by whether it is moving quickly and costing its leader money.

Rokag helps manage the Horde's defenses and logistics at Stonebreaker Hold while arakkoa attacks threaten its merchants, couriers, and soldiers. He wants the arakkoa leaders stopped and is wary of claims that some arakkoa are friendly to the Horde. When shown plans linking the fel orcs with the blood elves, he is surprised and troubled, and wonders why they are working together.

At Allerian Stronghold, Bertelm maps the forest and observes timber worgs, noting their fearlessness and defense of their territory. He is trying to make a cloak trimmed with worg tails and topped with the pelt of the elusive Ironjaw, which has repeatedly outsmarted his attempts to trap it. A map of the fel orcs' plans convinces him they serve the blood elves and are meant to keep the Alliance occupied; he says it raises more questions than it answers.

Thander is an officer at Allerian Stronghold who wants the nearby arakkoa settlements stopped before their attacks make the roads unsafe for merchants, couriers, and soldiers. He relies on scouts to identify the settlements’ leaders and directs a campaign against them, framing it as protection for local people and travelers.

Ros'eleth is a high elf at Allerian Stronghold who hopes to become a Farstrider, a childhood ambition she says she never outgrew. She works to help scattered high elves resist demonic magic, seeking magical vessels from Tuurem for that purpose. Her interest in the forest’s trees also leads her to collect Olemba seeds, wondering whether they could grow on Azeroth and hoping to send them to Stormwind’s park.

Warden Treelos is stationed at the Cenarion Thicket. His speech is fractured and unsettled: he asks who visitors are, wonders where everyone went, and shifts between accusations, theatrical lines, and confused remarks about dinner guests. In one account he fears Naphthal'ar’s unrelenting stare and asks a visitor to persuade it to come down for tea. His words suggest distress and confusion, but do not explain their cause.

Naphthal'ar is a solitary named creature in the Cenarion Thicket. Warden Treelos describes it as watching those nearby from the tower and warns that it dislikes jokes and foolishness; this account comes from Treelos, not Naphthal'ar.

Earthbinder Tavgren is a Cenarion druid investigating the massacre in the thicket, where he and one other druid survived. He suspects an unnatural cause, studies the changed teromoths for clues, and seeks information about what happened.

Tooki is a level 65 member of the Cenarion community at Stonebreaker Hold, where he helps investigate threats to the druids and the hold. He examines evidence from the attack, directs people to report findings to others, and celebrates when the threat to the hold ends. His speech uses a distinctive dialect.

Kokorek is an elderly arakkoa sage living in hiding at Veil Lithic. He helps an outsider overcome the wards protecting Veil Shalas so a captive friend can be rescued, while limiting his aid to that purpose. He describes his people’s lost former greatness and warns against repeating their past mistakes. He calls the ogres an ancient enemy of his people and asks for help dealing with one who provokes them.
A Shienor Talonite is one of the arakkoa forces at Veil Shienor, the nest attacked by Alliance forces in response to night raids.
A Shienor Sorcerer is a spellcaster among the arakkoa forces at Veil Shienor. The arakkoa use dark magic and summoning circles to rescue their warriors. This Sorcerer stays still while out of combat.
A Shienor Wing Guard is a guard posted among the Shienor. It fights with Shield Bash when an opponent comes within close range.
A Skithian Dreadhawk is a combatant found in the Skithian area. It holds position out of combat.
A Skithian Windripper is a combatant found in the Skithian area. It casts Arakkoa Blast in combat and Power of Kran'aish when it gains an opponent's attention.
A Shalassi Talonguard is a guard found in the Shalassi area. It uses Pierce Armor in combat.
A Shalassi oracle found in the Terokkar Forest. It uses Arakkoa Blast when fighting.
A Tuurem scavenger found around Tuurem in Terokkar Forest.
A Tuurem hunter found around Tuurem in Terokkar Forest. It keeps still while out of combat and uses ranged attacks.

Jenai Starwhisper is a Cenarion druid at the thicket who helps investigate its silence and the deaths of its druids. She recognizes bomb parts as part of an ethereal threat and sends word to the Allerian Post. After the danger passes, she celebrates the community's survival and praises the hero who helped secure it.
A lost spirit haunting the Bone Wastes beyond Auchindoun, where draenei spirits corrupted by the explosion wander in torment. It attacks with Cry of the Dead.
A Dampscale basilisk of Terokkar’s dry wilds, it brings its glare to bear when fighting.
A Dampscale devourer prowling Terokkar’s wilds, it uses a powerful chomp when fighting.
A warp stalker of Terokkar’s wilds.
A warp hunter prowling Terokkar.
A Dreadfang lurker prowling Terokkar’s wilds, it strikes with dread poison when fighting.
A Dreadfang widow of Terokkar, it strikes with dread poison when fighting.
Teromoths provide the unaffected comparison samples Earthbinder Tavgren needs to investigate the vicious creatures remaining in the Cenarion Thicket. Their combat repertoire includes Pacifying Dust.
Royal teromoths are beasts whose combat repertoire includes Pacifying Dust.

Bonelashers inhabit the Bone Wastes and gather at Carrion Hill. A bounty condemns them as plague carriers, while Mawg Grimshot seeks their destruction after a bite made him sick. Their combat repertoire includes Fevered Disease.

Mug'gok is an ogre whom Kokorek describes as adventurous but foolish, alternating between troubling friends at the Bleeding Hollow Ruins and provoking Kokorek's people. Mug'gok calls for the bird-men to come out and play, complains about hurt feelings and announces that he will find new friends when rebuffed. Kokorek demands his head as proof of good faith in a proposed rescue bargain.
A timber worg alpha, an animal distinguished by its furious howl in combat.

Empoor is a Broken merchant who deals in goods and information. During the local investigation, he is pressed to share what he knows; his replies show irritation and reluctance, including an exasperated protest and a declaration that he is leaving. His responses also reflect his busy work and the pressure he has endured.
Empoor's bodyguard accompanies the merchant as a protector. The guard can respond alongside Empoor when the encounter turns hostile.
A fallen druid among the bodies in Terokkar Forest.
Ashkaz is an arakkoa leader of Veil Reskk, one of the settlements whose leaders Thander’s scouts identify as threatening local Alliance traffic.
Ayit is an arakkoa leader of Veil Shienor, one of the settlements whose leaders Thander’s scouts identify as threatening local Alliance traffic.
Urdak is an arakkoa leader of Veil Skith, one of the settlements whose leaders Thander’s scouts identify as threatening local Alliance traffic.
The Firewing Courier guards Firewing property and objects to outsiders taking it, warning that the item belongs to Firewing Point.

Sharth Voldoun oversees Firewing Point’s mana-bomb project and holds its final codes. He reports that a smaller prototype succeeded at the Cenarion Thicket, a second bomb is being ritually fueled, and more parts are coming from Tuurem. He assures his master he will destroy nearby enemies, but reacts angrily when threatened in his quarters.

Theloria Shadecloak is an exiled high elf at Allerian Post. She is troubled by the fel-orc buildup near the post and works to contain it while investigating a blood-elf woman seen giving orders at the Bonechewer camp. She considers the Farstriders’ allegiance to Kael’thas a betrayal by former kin, and says the forest is now her only home.

Shadowstalker Kaide is a Horde operative watching the fel-orc presence near Stonebreaker Hold. He investigates Lisaile Fireweaver after observing her travel between the fel-orc stronghold and the blood-elf outpost, where he believes she is issuing orders to the fel-orc leader. His curiosity leads him to follow her close to the outpost, and he seeks to stop her before she returns. Kaide also wants the fel-orc threat contained quietly: he fears that news of failure will bring unwanted attention from Thrallmar and aims to keep the matter from spreading beyond Stonebreaker.

Lisaile Fireweaver is a blood elf liaison whom observers have seen traveling between Firewing Point and the fel-orc stronghold and speaking with its leader. Kaide reads her body language as evidence that she is issuing orders, though the orders' source and purpose remain unknown to him. She is sought before she can leave the fel-orc camp again. Her supplied records identify her as a level-64 creature and show combat behavior, but provide no further account of her motives or allegiances.

Floon is identified as one of Sal'salabim's debtors. The collection demand addresses him directly, and his recorded reply threatens violence: “I choose the third option: KILLING YOU!” His gossip text is a series of clicking and clucking sounds. The available records do not explain the debt's origin or provide further background on Floon.

A Warped Peon is one of the workers building and repairing the fel orc fortifications in the Bonechewer Ruins. Thander’s account describes the construction as ongoing day and night; these workers are targets in the effort to disrupt it. When badly wounded, a peon attempts to flee for help.
Deathskitter is a rare, named beast. It attacks with Dread Poison, giving it a dangerous presence in combat.

Stonegazer is a basilisk unusually old for its kind, known by name to Sha’nir since she was young. Sha’nir says it is rumored to live east of Shattrath near the edge of the land, and seeks its blood for a traditional cure intended to restore Zahlia’s lost sight.

Soolaveen is troubled by the restless dead in the Bone Wastes and urges others to ease their suffering. He asks for draenei bones to be taken to Ramdor for proper care, and thanks those who put the corrupted spirits to rest, treating the work as a humane release from torment.

Keb'ezil is Kurgatok's imp and was sent to investigate disturbances interrupting his master's spellcasting. Keb'ezil found that warp stalkers were disrupting the area's magical energy; Kurgatok describes the imp as one who talks back.

Taela Everstride is a high elf in the Alliance settlement of Allerian Stronghold. She handles the bonelasher bounty and offers a separate hunt for Torgos, the feared king of the bonelashers. Her interest in the hunt is practical: she wants Torgos's tail feather as proof. Taela's greeting shows she is amused and annoyed when mistaken for a blood elf, and she answers that confusion with dry sarcasm.

Mawg Grimshot wants revenge on the bonelashers: their bite left him with fainting spells, and he hates them for it. Torgos took one of Mawg's eyes during a hunt at Veil Rhaze, so Mawg now seeks the creature's death and asks for its tail feather as proof. His dialogue is blunt and openly resentful; he admits that his injury and spells keep him from hunting the bonelashers himself.

Advisor Faila helps oversee Stonebreaker Hold’s security. She sends Scout Neftis to investigate an unknown group at Grangol’var Village, fearing the Shadow Council could establish a stronghold near the Hold. She also directs action against arakkoa nests after their attacks, and receives Isla Starmane’s report about Firewing Point and the Cenarion Thicket.

Lieutenant Gravelhammer is responsible for security at Allerian Stronghold and favors proactive action to prevent surprise attacks. He directs Private Weeks to investigate a shadowy group at Grangol’var Village; after learning it is the Shadow Council, he orders a response against its leader and forces. He also calls for thinning the arakkoa attacking the area.

Scout Neftis is a field scout watching the shadowy group at Grangol'var Village. She wants to learn what they are doing and has observed that an initiate, a laborer and an advisor are willing to talk. Neftis provides a disguise for this investigation, warns that local hunters can see through it, and says it is fragile outside the village. Her report has gone to Stonebreaker Hold, whose response she has been waiting on.

Private Weeks is a field scout watching the shadowy group at Grangol'var Village from its north entrance. He wants to learn what they are doing and has observed that an initiate, a laborer and an advisor are willing to talk. Weeks provides a disguise for this investigation, warns that local hunters can see through it, and says it is fragile outside the village. His report has gone to the Allerian Stronghold, whose response he has been waiting on.

Shadowy Initiate is one of the hostile, chatty figures Weeks and Neftis have observed in Grangol'var. When approached, the Initiate protests that the interruption has forced a task to start over, suggesting focused work and impatience with the visitor.

Shadowy Laborer works on repairs for the Shadow Council in Grangol'var and says the Council does not pay him by the hour. He is busy and impatient when interrupted. Private Weeks and Scout Neftis identify him as one of the hostile village members they have observed speaking.

Weeks and Neftis describe Shadowy Advisor as one of the hostile, chatty figures they observed in Grangol'var. He says he is busy discussing important matters with his leader, demands that visitors be quick, and threatens them with a beating. His response presents him as an impatient, forceful participant in those discussions.

Shadowmaster Grieve leads the Shadow Council in a village in Terokkar Forest. He treats intruders with open hostility, warning that he may kill or sacrifice anyone who returns. His threats invoke Auchindoun’s labyrinth and Murmur, reflecting the danger he poses to those who challenge his authority.

Captain Auric Sunchaser commands at Allerian Stronghold, where Lieutenant Gravelhammer reports to him. Auric delegates urgent matters to his lieutenant and expects problems to be handled promptly. He also receives Isla Starmane’s report after her escape from Firewing Point, learning of the threat there and thanking those who brought her and her information to safety on the stronghold’s behalf.
Shimmerscale Eels are beasts recorded in the Terokkar Forest region.

Isla Starmane came to Outland from the Cenarion Expedition on a diplomatic mission and was captured at Firewing Point. She says she carries information vital to the security of the nearby hold, and seeks help escaping to deliver it. Her escort lines show determination to leave, while she pauses to ensure her helper is ready.
Kerna is a wind rider master who helps travelers arrange flights. She invites visitors to choose where they would like to fly; when attacked, she calls for guards.
Furnan Skysoar is a gryphon master who helps travelers arrange flights. He invites visitors to choose where they would like to fly; when attacked, he calls for help.

Isfar is an arakkoa driven to free his sister Lakka, whom his older brother Syth holds in the Sethekk Halls. Once part of the Sethekk, Isfar came to doubt Syth and Ikiss and carries guilt over his former people's crimes. He seeks to restore Terokk's stolen relics to Skettish honor, and hopes to return home only when Lakka is free.
Innkeeper Grilka offers the services expected at an inn: a place to rest, lodging, and goods. Her inn talk welcomes battle weary visitors to lay down their weapons and share stories.
Dod'ss is a general goods merchant in the local settlement, offering goods for visitors to browse.
Rungor is a trade goods merchant in the local settlement, offering goods for visitors to browse.

Bar Talet is a bowyer in Allerian Stronghold, serving as a vendor who offers goods and repairs equipment. His role is tied to the bowyer trade, giving visitors a practical source of supplies and gear maintenance.
A Stonebreaker grunt in Terokkar Forest.
Trag is a stable master who helps travelers manage their pets and recover lost companions.

An Allerian Defender on duty, this guard talks with fellow defenders about a wanted poster offering gold for killing bonelashers. The conversation moves between curiosity about the bounty, concern about the dangerous Bone Wastes and its disease-carrying creatures, and the prospect of earning extra money after a shift. The defenders also complain that adventurers are paid for work they already do, revealing a wry sense of unfairness alongside their caution.
A high elf ranger.
Gardok Ripjaw is a humanoid found in Terokkar Forest.
An Allerian horseman in Terokkar Forest.
Supply Officer Mills is a rations vendor stationed in Allerian Stronghold. His title and stock mark him as a quartermaster figure supplying provisions to the outpost.
Leeli Longhaggle sells trade goods in Allerian Stronghold. Her name and trade-goods counter identify her as a local merchant serving the outpost.
A Stonebreaker peon in Terokkar Forest.
Fabian Lanzonelli runs the general goods and bags counter in Allerian Stronghold. His shop marks him as a practical supplier to the outpost.
Cecil Meyers supplies blacksmithing materials and offers repairs. His combined trade and repair services make him a practical contact for local smiths.
An Allerian peasant, one of the ordinary people of the region.
An orc refugee, displaced from home and encountered among the people of the region.
Soot is a critter encountered in Terokkar.
An Allerian peasant, one of the ordinary people of the region.
Lemla Hopewing is an apprentice gryphon master. When she is attacked, an enraged gryphon is summoned.
Innkeeper Biribi greets visitors with a question about resting or taking a meal.
An ancient draenei spirit.

Ramdor the Mad is a former death priest excommunicated for beliefs he presents as common sense: the dead should be left alone rather than subjected to Maladaar's necromancy. He promises proper burials and urges putting tormented spirits to rest, though he grumbles at more bones. Ramdor lures help with a claim of hidden treasures, then admits he lied to obtain Ezekiel's book. He is also unsettled by a child communing with a grandfather and the mother's untroubled response.

Spy Grik'tha works under disguise for Shattrath's Lower City coalition and asks potential attackers to hold their blows. Grik'tha fears for To'gun, who returned to the Shadow Labyrinth to gather information and rescue other spies despite losses. Torn between affection and anger at the risk, Grik'tha suspects Shadow Council magic exposed the operation and asks brave visitors to search for the missing colleague.
An operative of Shattrath's Lower City coalition.
A Lower City healer, identified by that healing role and affiliation.
A Cabal agent in the Lower City area.

Field Commander Mahfuun is a commander among the Lower City's free people, directing resistance to the Shadow Council in Auchindoun. He has spies inside and says his forces will hold the agents while an adventurer enters the Shadow Labyrinth to investigate. He is frustrated by delayed help and the continuing danger after Auchindoun's explosion.

Grek is an orc weapon professional in Shattrath's Lower City, known for blunt, simple speech and inability to read. A wanted poster prompts him to ask for help and offer to help in return. He tests Rakoria's weapon oil, then rejects it as unsuitable for him, insisting he is no weakling in robes.
Grek's Riding Wolf is a wolf associated with Grek and present in the same Shattrath area.
A great elekk of Outland.

Mamdy presents himself as an “ologist” who studies everything and boasts that he is the most intelligent ethereal one could meet. He then catches himself: that boast, he admits, was the dealer in him speaking.

Artificer Morphalius has a plan to break his crew’s deadlock at the Mana-Tombs: clear a route through Shaffar’s ethereals, then activate a transporter so the crew can get inside. He offers a reward for the work.
Consortium Laborers are the Consortium’s workforce for physical work.
Consortium Engineers are the Consortium’s technical workforce.

Nexus-Prince Haramad treats the Mana-Tombs as a contest for profit: he recruits help against Shaffar, dismisses the rival’s defenses, and offers a reward for Shaffar’s defeat. He mocks outsiders as “flesh beasts” and invites them to seek work at the Stormspire, which he calls home. His greeting jokes that would-be killers should take a number.

“Captain” Kaftiz is working to break the ward that blocks other ethereal groups from entering Shaffar’s domain. He says he has top ethereals on the job and expects the way in to open soon, so his immediate concern is getting his group through the defenses to claim what they seek.

“Slim” is a Consortium-friendly dealer whose quoted name irritates him: he calls both “Slim” and “Shady” insulting and bluntly threatens an unwelcome visitor. When addressing a Consortium friend, he turns to business and offers a purchase.
A Draenei pilgrim in the Auchindoun area.
Clarissa is grieving and asks to be left alone.

Ha’lei is a child who says she sees dead draenei, though others dismiss her. She points to Ramdor as someone who sees ghosts too, and finds it funny that adults call him crazy while they pat her on the head. Her quest text presents her as believing her visions and hoping she never grows up.

Greatfather Aldrimus is a fortunate spirit outside the Auchenai Crypts, spared both Levixus’s binding and Maladaar’s necromantic experiments. He asks that Maladaar be destroyed so the spirits trapped inside can rest in peace; he describes himself as lacking a material form and says he can offer items from the spirit world.
Provisioner Tsaalt welcomes friends of the Lower City, warns that fighting is underway inside and his compatriots need help, and suggests doing business may be possible for a friend of the district.

Spirit Sage Gartok has encountered Spirit Shards in his travels but has not unlocked their secrets; he believes they originate in Auchindoun's depths and is interested in acquiring any shards others find.

Spirit Sage Zran has encountered Spirit Shards in his travels but has not unlocked their secrets; he believes they originate in Auchindoun's depths and is interested in acquiring any shards others find.

Levixus, the Soul Caller, is a necromancer who reads from the Book of the Dead and uses demonic ritual to call the dead by name and bind tortured souls to his will. He threatens to raise all of Auchindoun.
Horvon is a draenei armorsmith whose passion for armorcrafting endures in life and death. He asks strangers to treat him as if he were living and invites them to let him repair their items.

Terokkarantula is described as the brood-mother of the dreadfang widows, lairing deep within Netherweb Ridge. Vindicator Haylen identifies her as the source of the widows threatening the area; she fights with crippling and dread poison.
A Skettis refugee is among the displaced people.
A human refugee is among the displaced people.
A Shattrath refugee in Terokkar Forest.
Siflaed Coldhammer is a tinker in Shattrath, where she sells goods and offers repairs. Her trade gives travelers practical help with equipment and supplies.
Skraa is a trade-goods vendor in Shattrath. The trade-goods label marks her stock apart from the general supplies and food sold by nearby merchants.
Ruogo sells general goods in Shattrath, providing everyday supplies alongside the more specialized trade goods and provisions offered by nearby merchants.
Morula is a food and drink vendor in Shattrath. Her shop provides provisions distinct from the general goods and trade supplies sold by nearby merchants.
Miihi is a humanoid in Terokkar Forest.
Miiji is a humanoid in Terokkar Forest.
Dealer Tariq is a merchant titled Shady Dealer who offers goods for sale.

Lieutenant Meridian wants to take the fight to the enemies surrounding Allerian Stronghold. Confirmation that Firewing Point is building a mana bomb vindicates suspicions he had hoped were wrong. His intelligence points to Sharth Voldoun holding its final code; he orders the bomb detonated to protect the stronghold.

Sergeant Chawni expects visitors to make themselves useful and complains that the nearby shadowstalker is doing little. She directs attacks on Firewing Point and wants its mana bomb detonated to protect Stonebreaker Hold. Confirmation of the bomb parts vindicates suspicions she had hoped were wrong.
Thadok is a humanoid in Terokkar Forest.
Kugnar is a humanoid in Terokkar Forest.
Gralga’s idle remark links learning to read with having a drink, ending with an invitation to toast.
Ru'zah is a humanoid in Terokkar Forest.

Deathtalon Spirits are hostile spirits associated with the ruined Skettis settlement of Veil Rhaze, where Terokk's influence endured after the village's destruction. Kirrik the Awakened identifies them among the murderous spirits there and sends the player to fight them as an early blow against Terokk and Skettis's guardians. They bear spirit particles on respawn.
A hostile spirit lingering at Veil Rhaze under Terokk's influence, the Screeching Spirit attacks with fear.
An Auchenai death-speaker who holds position outside combat and maintains Demon Armor, serving as a spellcasting combatant.

A Bonechewer Messenger follows a patrol route, breaking into a run and later slowing. It warns, “Be on your guard! The enemy is on the prowl.” Its route and alerts mark it as a lookout carrying news of nearby enemies.
A Bonechewer Marauder is a Bonechewer raider encountered in Terokkar Forest.
A pink elekk, a beast found in Terokkar Forest.
Harbinger Ardonan is a named herald in Outland.

An Auchenai soldier serving in the Bone Wastes. Commander Ra'vaj describes the growing Auchenai force as overwhelming his troops and asks that its soldiers be kept occupied while scouts investigate their activity.

An Auchenai doomsayer serving among the force in the Bone Wastes. Commander Ra'vaj identifies the Auchenai as soldiers threatening his outpost; this doomsayer's combat magic includes Mind Blast and Mind Flay.
A dead clefthoof found in the Bone Wastes.
Aimi is a named individual found in the Bone Wastes.

A spirit raven among the murderous spirits haunting Veil Rhaze, a ruined Skettis settlement. Kirrik the Awakened identifies these spirits as part of Terokk's lingering influence and sends travelers to destroy them.

An ethereal plunderer haunting the Tomb of Lights, where ethereals scavenge keepsakes from the dead. High Priest Orglum calls this a profanation of the burial place; the plunderer's combat technique includes Backstab.
An ethereal hostile presence in the Tomb of Lights, the Nethermancer is among the ethereals looting keepsakes from the dead. It attacks with Shadow Bolt.
Aeman Brightsong celebrates a group's salvation with wine, calling it a fine vintage and applauding lightly. His remarks suggest relief and a taste for celebratory wine.
Theine Brightsong is a humanoid in Terokkar Forest.
Erick Nateson is a humanoid in Terokkar Forest.
Eckert reacts to the group's rescue with exuberant relief, asking if they are really saved before declaring it time to party.
An ethereal arcanist found in the Tomb of Lights, this hostile caster holds position out of combat and is encountered among the tomb's ethereal threat.

David Wayne is a human smith who left the Sons of Lothar after joining the Draenor expedition and now works at Wayne’s Refuge. He is remaking an anti-demon sword, planning its construction around unusual materials, demon wards and a heat source powerful enough for the ingots. He explains the weapon’s enchantments and guides the player through gathering its components and quenching the finished blade, acknowledging the effort involved.

Trachela is a named bonelashers’ mate whose carcass can be used to lure Torgos from the protection of Torgos’s Bane. Mawg Grimshot and Taela Everstride both describe her at Carrion Hill; her own combat behavior includes casting Fevered Disease.
Afrazi Forest Strider is a creature.

Vengeful Draenei are draenei dead corrupted by the Shadow Council in the Tomb of Lights, left as cursed spirits angry and confused, with hatred for the living. High Priest Orglum asks adventurers to defeat them and grant these tragic victims rest.

The Vengeful Harbinger represents the cursed draenei spirits of the Tomb of Lights. After their torment ends, the Harbinger says many have been saved from an eternity of darkness, acknowledges having little to offer the living, and invites them to take what seems useful.
Skettis Wing Guards are winged humanoid guards associated with Skettis. They can enter a frenzy in combat and use a combat ability against opponents.
A Skettis Windwalker is a Skettis combatant who attacks with Arcane Bolt and Cyclone. When a nearby ally is badly hurt, it can cast Shadow Mend to help.
A Skettis Talonite is a Skettis combatant.
A Time-Lost Skettis Reaver is a combatant found around Skettis. It uses a combat spell.
A Skettis Time-Shifter is a Skettis combatant whose attacks include spells.
A Cabal Abjurist is a Cabal combatant who uses Arcane Missiles and Frost Nova against hostile targets.

A Cabal skirmisher, one of the Shadow Council cabal cultists threatening the Refugee Caravan near Auchindoun. In combat, this attacker can become enraged, warns that its prey will not escape, and threatens them with death.
A Cabal tomb-raider encountered around Auchindoun. This hostile cabal fighter attacks with Backstab, fitting its role as a close-quarters raider.
A Blackwind sabercat prowling the wilds around Skettis. This large feline attacks with a rending bite, relying on its claws and teeth rather than speech or services.
A Skettis Surger, an elemental presence in the Skettis region. Its name and elemental nature distinguish it from the local humanoid worshippers and cabal fighters.
Alluvion is a powerful water elemental found in Skettis. It holds its ground until provoked, then attacks with Water Bolt.
A Time-Lost Skettis worshipper: a humanoid figure found among the ruins and wilds of Skettis.

A Time-Lost Skettis High Priest is an arakkoa spellcaster found in Skettis. In combat, this priest uses Shadow Word: Pain and Holy Smite, and can cast Flash Heal on an injured ally, showing both offensive magic and support for nearby allies.
Skettis Kaliri are wild birds found around Skettis. They defend themselves by swooping at attackers.
Ironspine Chompers are wild beasts found around Terokkar Forest. They attack by biting, as their name and combat ability suggest.

A slain Auchenai warrior lies among the battlefield dead in the Bone Wastes. Commander Ra'vaj says the Auchenai and Sha'tar dead are being taken for their souls and orders their bodies burned to keep them from being used in the Auchenai's rituals.
Bone Crawlers tunnel through the bone fields, lying in wait beneath the surface. When roused, one stops tunneling, sheds its passive concealment, and attacks with Bore and poison.
An Auchenai Warrior is a combatant of the Auchenai, armed for close fighting and able to unleash a Whirlwind in battle.
Ironspine Petrifiers are creatures found across the Bone Wastes. Their name and combat use of Glare mark them as a distinct kind of local wildlife.
Sha'tar Vindicators are elite Sha'tar fighters stationed across the Bone Wastes. Their name and battlefield deployment mark them as defenders of the Sha'tar presence there.
Unliving Guardians patrol the Bone Wastes as roaming sentries.
An undead initiate encountered in the Auchindoun region.

A Cabal Spell-weaver is one of the hostile cabal attackers south of the Refugee Caravan near Auchindoun. In combat it casts Incinerate and, when badly wounded, Drain Life. Mekeda's quest names spell-weavers among the attackers.

A Cabal Initiate is among the hostile cabal attackers south of the Refugee Caravan near Auchindoun. This one fights with Eviscerate and can be seen going into a frenzy. Mekeda's quest identifies initiates among the attackers.
A Skettis Soulcaller holds its ground outside combat and answers attackers with Shadow Bolt, a dark spell fitting its role as one of Skettis’s callers.
Skettis Sentinels stand watch across the region. In combat, this sentinel casts spells, including abilities triggered as it is wounded.
An Accursed Apparition appears in Terokkar Forest; when it returns, it activates stealth detection.

npcs.name: Terokkar Forest - Shadow Council Invisible Stalker

records.text: A Shadow Council invisible stalker is an unseen presence in Terokkar Forest.
An Auchenai Death-Spirit, a spirit of the dead associated with the Auchenai, appears in Terokkar Forest.
Skettis Eviscerators appear across several areas of Skettis. When combat begins, an Eviscerator uses Throw against its opponent.
Vengeful Husk is an undead combatant encountered in Outland.
When an Infested Root-Walker dies, it casts a spell that summons wood mites, linking the creature's infestation to a further danger nearby.
In combat, a Scorpid Bonecrawler uses a venom sting.
Decrepit Clefthooves are combat creatures that can stomp. One has a frenzy emote, suggesting its agitation is visible to nearby onlookers.
Gordunni Back-Breakers are members of the Gordunni group. In combat they can kick, and a frenzy emote signals their agitation.
Gordunni Elementalists belong to the Gordunni group. One raises a Lightning Shield when it gains an enemy's attention, showing a readiness to defend itself with elemental magic.
Gordunni Head-Splitters are ogre fighters found in the Barrier Hills. They use a cleaving attack in combat and can enrage when badly wounded.

Slaag, one of Gruul's sons, exiled himself and took control of the Gordunni ogres in the Barrier Hills. A solitary, powerful ogre, he is identified by his own standard, which outsiders seek as proof that he has been dealt with. In combat he can enrage and enter a frenzy.

Kirrik is an arakkoa who rejected Terokk as a false prophet and led fellow dissenters out of Skettis. He later searched the colonies for others and now leads the Refugee Caravan. He serves A'dal's Light, hoping to redeem arakkoa still under Terokk's influence, while judging those wholly in Terokk's grasp beyond redemption and calling for their destruction.

High Priest Orglum is a spiritual leader with the Refugee Caravan. He came to Outland to cleanse troubled spirits, but the caravan’s attack left him worried about those lost in the wastes and unable to pursue his mission. He describes the Tomb of Lights as a resting place now troubled by ethereals and cursed dead, and directs others to confront those threats. His words also show gratitude toward those who help protect his people.
A quest target in Terokkar Forest.
The Rotting Forest-Rager is a beast found in several areas of Terokkar Forest. When it dies, it casts a spell that summons Wood Mites, linking its death to the appearance of smaller creatures.
The Captive Child is among the children held in Veil Skith. The child speaks with fear about the “weird bird guys,” worries that the captives might be eaten, and celebrates when they are free.
An Arakkoa fly target in Terokkar Forest.
Netherweb Victim is a passive webbed creature.

Scout Navrin serves the Sha'tari Base Camp amid the dangers of the Bone Wastes. After Netherweb Ridge spiders poisoned and carried off Sha'tar warriors, he sought help finding survivors; when rescued warriors could not return because of dreadfang poison, he arranged a rescue party. He speaks of the wastes as a place where dangers and ambushes are ever possible.

Ethan is a child among the stranded refugees at the Refugee Caravan. Frightened by the night attack that halted their journey, he worries about friends taken by the bird men and asks for help finding them. He misses having children to play with and offers one of his toys in thanks when they are reunited.

Mekeda is a Broken among the refugees at the Refugee Caravan, fearful of another Cabal attack. They distrust the guards’ confidence and urge resistance before the cultists strike again. Mekeda knows some Shadow Council cipher from life among Lower City outcasts and refugees, though admits their skill is imperfect. They also honor the sacred relics of their people and remember the Light despite feeling it has forgotten them; Auchindoun’s spirits are their ancestors.
Akuno is a refugee trying to escape the cultists pursuing him. Grateful for help, he urges a quick departure and says his friend Mekeda will reward those who aided him.
The Cabal Interrogator questions a refugee about the caravan's presence in the Bone Wastes and attacks Akuno with a kick.
Hathyss the Wicked scorns a group scrambling like rats and laments that Auchindoun should have belonged to them.
The Lithic Oracle is a combatant whose magic includes blasts, shocks and lightning, as well as a power called Power of Kran'aish.
The Lithic Talonguard is a guard-type combatant whose attacks can pierce armor.
A defender associated with the Refugee Caravan area of Terokkar Forest, serving the caravan's protection.

Lakotae is a named figure at the Refugee Caravan who calls attention to the damage ravaging Terokkar's trees. He asks for help clearing wood mites from the forest-ragers and root-walkers east of the caravan, hoping the worst of the infestation can be brought under control.

Skywing is a flying creature who can speak. After being freed from a curse, he asks that Rilak the Redeemed be told he is safe and declares his mission in Skettis: defeat Terokk. During his escort, he signals the way by flying ahead and pausing at landmarks.

Teribus the Cursed is a named demon called forth as the opponent in a necromantic ritual. The Dread Relic and doom skulls let challengers command him to face them, making him the ritual's dangerous target.

Commander Ra’vaj is strained by the Sha’tar’s losses and the Auchenai’s campaign to seize the dead and use their souls. He refuses to let either side’s fallen feed the enemy’s rituals, and pushes for action against the Auchenai while his scouts investigate their plans. Even after a new discovery, he remains troubled that the effort may not be enough.
An injured Sha’tar Vindicator, a wounded defender marked out from the order’s able-bodied fighters.

Oakun knows the Dread Relic is evil and warns that carrying it risks both life and soul, yet sees it as central to confronting Teribus the Cursed. Oakun directs the use of Auchenai doom skulls to empower the relic and draw Teribus into a challenge, then asks whether the threat has been purged from Terokkar’s skies.

Chief Archaeologist Letoll leads an Explorers' League crew and hires protection for their digs. Letoll gives brisk, colloquial orders to keep the crew organized and expects a bodyguard to keep every employee safe. Dwarfowitz handles payment for a successful expedition.

Vindicator Haylen is a senior Sha’tar defender left gravely poisoned after the Dreadfang Widows overwhelmed his companions west of Netherweb Ridge. Devoted to the naaru, he asks for help avenging the fallen and rescuing those taken; news of victory gives him hope, though he fears the poison will kill him before he can free the others.
A wounded Sha’tar defender in the Bone Wastes, identified as a Vindicator of the Sha’tar.
An Explorers’ League researcher with the dig crew in the Bone Wastes. He treats finding a drum as a remarkable archaeological discovery, but is already keen to leave the desert.
Aundro supplies blacksmithing goods in Terokkar Forest and can also repair equipment.
Anchorite Ensham is a first aid trainer in Terokkar Forest. He offers instruction and points learners toward Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen in Theramore for further training.

Dwarfowitz leads the Explorers' League expedition at Sha'tari Base Camp and is absorbed by the bone worms of the Bone Wastes. He sends out researchers with fumping drums and gathers carcasses to study the creatures, convinced their work is nearing a breakthrough. Reports of sand gnomes draw his dry skepticism.
A Lost Torranche is a beast that tries to flee for help when badly wounded.
A Cenarion sparrowhawk guides the player toward a buried raven stone, then searches the ground and locates one. It is a working bird.
A Skyguard scout stationed in Skettis.

A Skyguard navigator in Skettis who greets familiar flyers as an ace and jokes about their speed, mount, and rough flights. The banter suggests easy familiarity with experienced fliers, without establishing a deeper relationship.
A Skyguard nether ray, an animal found across several Outland regions.
The Skyguard Handler is a humanoid in Skettis.
Gordunni Soulreaper is an elite humanoid combatant. Its attacks include Shadow Bolt, summoning skeletons, and Drain Life.
Talonsworn Forest-Rager is an elite beast found in the Skettis region. Its combat behavior includes Thunderclap.

Sky Commander Adaris commands forces confronting the arakkoa at Skettis. Seriously wounded, he drifts in and out of consciousness but remains intent on breaking the enemy's chain of command. He distrusts the risk of helping Rilak bring Terokk back and fears endorsing the plan could provoke mutiny; he nevertheless authorizes it and commits his men to support, warning that failure may leave only one chance.

Severin is a Skyguard medic caring for the badly wounded Sky Commander Adaris. He doubts Adaris's belief that shadow dust can reveal the arakkoa's hidden leaders, but gives him an elixir to humor him and follows his orders to prepare more. His skepticism is practical, and he remains attentive to the commander's condition.

Sky Sergeant Doryn is a Skyguard sergeant stationed outside Skettis at Blackwind Landing. He directs recruits against the arakkoa threat, including attacks on the hatcheries guarded by monstrous kaliri. He values rescuing scouts and putting supplies to use, and tests new recruits in the air.
Monstrous kaliri are oversized arakkoa attack birds used against Skyguard scouts. They guard hatcheries above Skettis and can knock riders from their mounts; one recorded combat tactic is Hamstring.

Talonpriest Ishaal is one of three Skettis clerics called talonpriests, sought out at Veil Ala'rak with the aid of an elixir of shadows. In combat he uses Flash Heal, Rejuvenation and Shadow Word: Pain.
Talonpriest Skizzik is one of three Skettis clerics called talonpriests, sought out at Veil Ala'rak with the aid of an elixir of shadows. In combat he uses Mind Flay and Psychic Scream.

A talonpriest cleric of Skettis, Zellek is one of three talonpriests identified as part of the Skettis chain of command. The account places him among the talonpriests who dwell in Veil Ala'rak, near Blackwind Lake; he fights with head-smashing and life-draining magic.
A disciple of Sar'this in Terokkar Forest, this follower is identified by allegiance to Sar'this rather than by a personal name.
An evoker associated with Sar'this, this figure is identified by magical role and allegiance. The evoker is in Terokkar Forest.
Sar'this is a figure in Terokkar Forest. Sar'this casts Summon Arcane Elemental.
A minion of Sar'this, this follower is identified by service to Sar'this and appears among the group in Terokkar Forest.
Blackwind Warp Chasers are beasts found in several areas of Shadowmoon Valley. They have a peculiar ability to turn invisible when they reset in normal dungeons.
The Skyguard Windcharger greets visiting fliers as fellow high-flyers, salutes the player as an officer, and suggests a race. Its banter gives it a jaunty, competitive air.

Hazzik is an arakkoa who says Terokk's talonpriests once would have sacrificed him as a low-caste member. He secretly crafts disguises for ethereal smugglers seeking rare books, and offers a package to help thwart the talonpriests' attempt to restore Terokk even if that defies your leader. He warns that the disguise will not fool other arakkoa.

Sahaak is an old, sickly arakkoa scribe and Keeper of Scrolls at Terokk's Rest. Nearly blind, he keeps apart from the war and pleads not to be harmed; when he mistakes a visitor for a young hatchling, he offers exotic texts for sale.
Grella is a Skyguard quartermaster at Blackwind Landing, where she supplies and repairs the equipment of the Sha'tari Skyguard.

A Skyguard Ace is a veteran aerial combatant in the fight against Terokk's forces at Skettis. The ace calls out enemy sightings and bombing maneuvers, directs support for ground troops, and reports when the enemy is defeated or Skyguard forces have fallen.

The Skyguard Prisoner is a captured Skyguard scout who was knocked from a nether ray during a mission over Skettis. After receiving help, the prisoner asks to escape the area and worries about remaining there; the scout expects Sergeant Doryn to welcome the return of a missing member of his team.

Skyguard Handler Deesak manages nether ray transport from Blackwind Landing and worries about the strain of the Skettis campaign on the animals: frequent sorties and feed shortages leave them at risk of exhaustion or starvation. Deesak also handles requests to feed a hungry ray and return to report on its care.
A Concert Bruiser is a tough security combatant associated with the concert in Blade's Edge. Its designation identifies a protective role.

Exorcist Sullivan is a named exorcist involved in the Alliance effort to secure a spirit tower in the Bone Wastes. The work seeks the favor of Auchindoun’s restless spirits, whose peace and customs matter even amid the Alliance-Horde conflict.

Exorcist Vaisha is a named exorcist involved in the Horde effort to secure a Spirit Tower in the Bone Wastes. The work seeks peace for Auchindoun’s restless spirits while competing with the Alliance for their favor; Vaisha’s role sits within that struggle despite the spirits’ lack of allegiance.
Leassian is a stable master who tends to travelers’ animal companions. Leassian offers help with stabling pets and recovering lost companions.
Razorthorn Flayers are creatures encountered in the Hellfire region. They attack in combat and cast a spell when fighting.
The Razorthorn Ravager is a creature found in the Hellfire region. It attacks in combat and uses Ravage against its opponent.

Old Man Barlo is an experienced fisherman who shares practical knowledge of fish habits and waters. He recalls an enormous mudfish that snapped his line years ago and eagerly hopes another angler can catch it. His humor includes calling the escaped fish a “son of a carp” and teasing about cooking a mean baby crocolisk before admitting the joke with a sly wink.
The Terokkar Forest Flame Warden is an Alliance-side attendant for the festival fires. He urges people to honor Alliance flames and desecrate Horde fires, which he calls unworthy.
The Terokkar Forest Flame Keeper is a Horde-side attendant for the festival fires. She urges people to honor Horde flames and desecrate Alliance fires, which she calls unworthy.
The ghostly Aldor celebrant welcomes the chance to visit friends and family again, celebrating together and sharing old stories.
The ghostly Scryer celebrant welcomes the chance to visit friends and family again, celebrating together and sharing old stories.

Cheerful Aldor Spirit is an otherwise invisible spirit who reunites with friends and family in Shattrath's graveyard during the holiday. The spirit remembers celebrating and sharing stories, and cheerfully asks for more Bread of the Dead after eating everything family had made. The quest text points players to Chapman for the recipe; the spirit thanks them for the bread and offers a small holiday gift.

Cheerful Scryer Spirit is an otherwise invisible spirit who reunites with friends and family in Shattrath's graveyard during the holiday. The spirit remembers celebrating and sharing stories, and cheerfully asks for more Bread of the Dead after eating everything family had made. The quest text points players to Chapman for the recipe; the spirit thanks them for the bread and offers a small holiday gift.
Crown Underlings are targets in the Crown investigation east of Shattrath in Terokkar Forest. The investigation directs players to rough them up and destroy a chemical wagon.

place_records.text: You are in Terokkar Forest, a contested wood in Outland where both the Alliance and the Horde hold settlements. Stonebreaker Hold is Horde and Allerian Stronghold is Alliance, while Auchindoun and Sha'tari Base Camp belong to neither side. Timber worgs, warp stalkers and warped peons roam the land, and arakkoa raid the roads.

You are in Cenarion Thicket, a grove in Terokkar Forest where druids were massacred and only two survived. Earthbinder Tavgren investigates the killings, comparing the changed teromoths with unaffected ones, while Warden Treelos is still stationed here, his speech fractured. Vicious teromoths and Naphthal'ar, a creature watching from the tower, make the grove dangerous.
You are in Tuurem, a stretch of Terokkar Forest on the road to Shattrath City. Tuurem scavengers and hunters prowl it, along with wrekt seers and wrekt warriors, and firewing couriers are seen here.
You are in Veil Shienor, an arakkoa settlement in Terokkar Forest. Shienor talonites, sorcerers and wing guards hold it, and Alliance officers want its leader Ayit killed so the roads stay safe.

You are in Veil Skith, an arakkoa settlement in Terokkar Forest where children are held captive. Skithian windrippers and dreadhawks hold the ground, Urdak is its leader and is marked for death, and a captive child there is frightened of the weird bird guys.
You are in Veil Shalas, a place in Terokkar Forest. Shalassi oracles and talonguards are hostile here, and an Okrek roams among them.

You are in Skettis, a time-lost place in Terokkar Forest where an arakkoa high priest casts both shadow and healing magic. Blackwind sabercats, skettis surgers and wing guards are hostile around it, and monstrous kaliri birds are a danger. A spirit healer is here too.

You are in Blackwind Valley, a stretch of Terokkar Forest where Blackwind sabercats, skettis surgers and skettis wing guards roam. A Cenarion sparrowhawk works the ground here, searching for buried raven stones.

You are in Firewing Point, a Terokkar Forest site where firewing warlocks, bloodwarders and defenders are hostile. Isla Starmane, a diplomat from the Cenarion Expedition, was captured here and wants out, carrying information she says is vital to the security of nearby holds.

You are in Grangol'var Village, a Terokkar Forest village where a shadowy group, the Shadow Council, has gathered. Horde scout Neftis and Alliance private Weeks both watch it, and shadowy summoners and executioners are hostile here. Shadowmaster Grieve leads them.

You are in Stonebreaker Hold, a Horde hold in Terokkar Forest. Advisor Faila oversees its security, and Rokag directs its defenses against arakkoa attacks on merchants and couriers. Kurgatok the warlock studies the arakkoa here, and Kerna, a wind rider master, arranges flights from its inn.

You are in Allerian Stronghold, an Alliance hold in Terokkar Forest. Lady Dena Kennedy is worried about arakkoa raids on supply lines, and Lieutenant Gravelhammer plans against surprise attacks. Andarl, a mage, suspects warp stalkers are making his spells fizzle, and Furnan Skysoar, a gryphon master, arranges flights from the hold.

You are in Bonechewer Ruins, a ruin in Terokkar Forest where fel orcs work day and night rebuilding fortifications. Bonechewer backbreakers and devastators and warped peons are hostile here. Plans found here suggest that blood elves at Firewing Point are giving the fel orcs their orders.
You are in Veil Lithic, a district of Terokkar Forest. Kokorek, an elderly arakkoa sage, lives in hiding here. Lithic oracles, talonguards and warp hunters roam the area and are the main dangers.

You are in Auchindoun, the ruined mausoleum of Terokkar Forest, held by neither side. Isfar, an arakkoa, wants to free his sister Lakka from his brother Syth in the Sethekk Halls. Lower City spies and Field Commander Mahfuun's resistance work against the Shadow Council here. Auchenai initiates, bonelashers and cabal agents are the dangers, and there is a spirit healer, repairs and a vendor.

You are in Veil Reskk, a district of Terokkar Forest. Shienor talonites, wing guards and sorcerers are the main dangers, along with ironspine petrifiers and dreadfang lurkers. Teromoths live here too and use Pacifying Dust in combat.

You are in Blackwind Lake, a lake in Terokkar Forest. Skettis kaliri birds swoop at anyone who attacks them. Skettis surgers and monstrous kaliri are the main dangers, with blackwind sabercats and alluvions also about.
You are in Lake Jorune, a lake in Terokkar Forest. Disciples and minions of Sar'this gather here, along with an evoker of Sar'this. Sar'this himself summons arcane elementals.
You are in Skethyl Mountains, a range in Terokkar Forest. Blackwind sabercats and skettis surgers hunt here, and blackwind warp chasers roam with them.

You are in The Barrier Hills, hills in Terokkar Forest with a spirit healer. Gordunni back-breakers, elementalists and head-splitters are the main dangers, with marsh dredgers and marsh lurkers too. Sporelok humanoids are found here.

You are in The Bone Wastes, a battlefield in Terokkar Forest beyond Auchindoun's walls. Lost spirits and broken skeletons wander the field, while dreadfang widows, infested root-walkers and scorpid bonecrawlers are the main dangers. Vindicator Haylen lies gravely poisoned and asks for help avenging his fallen companions.
You are in Bleeding Hollow Ruins, ruins in Terokkar Forest. Boulderfist invaders gather here in numbers, and Unkor the Ruthless lurks among them.

You are in Silmyr Lake, a lake in Terokkar Forest, northeast of Shattrath City. Old Man Barlo, Master of Fishing, fishes here and recalls an enormous mudfish that snapped his line and escaped. Shimmerscale eels and dampscale basilisks are the dangers here.

You are in Raastok Glade, a glade in Terokkar Forest with a spirit healer. Royal teromoths use Pacifying Dust in battle among timber worg alphas, warp stalkers and dampscale devourers, which are the main dangers.

You are in Netherweb Ridge, a ridge in Terokkar Forest where the Terokkarantula, brood-mother of the dreadfang widows, has her lair deep within. Netherweb victims, dreadfang widows, infested root-walkers and rotting forest-ragers are the main dangers.
You are in Derelict Caravan, a place in Terokkar Forest. Vengeful husks and accursed apparitions haunt it.

You are in the Refugee Caravan, a camp of stranded refugees in the Bone Wastes of Terokkar Forest. Kirrik the Awakened, an arakkoa who broke with Skettis, leads them, and High Priest Orglum is among the people here. A night attack halted their journey, and Mekeda fears the Cabal will strike again. Dead clefthoofs wander nearby, and Lakotae says wood mites are ravaging the trees to the east.
You are in Shadow Tomb, a tomb in Terokkar Forest. Cabal skirmishers, abjurists and tomb-raiders haunt it.

You are in Veil Rhaze, a former colony of Skettis in Terokkar Forest. Terokk's influence lingers in its maligned spirits, and screeching spirits, deathtalon spirits, spirit ravens and dreadfang widows prowl there.
You are in Tomb of Lights, a tomb in Terokkar Forest. Ethereal nethermancers and plunderers haunt it, along with a vengeful draenei.
You are in Carrion Hill, a hill in Terokkar Forest. Bonelashers gather there in numbers, with cripplers, bone crawlers and warp hunters.
You are in Writhing Mound, a mound in Terokkar Forest. Auchenai doomsayers and death-speakers roam it, and broken skeletons lie among them.

You are in the Ring of Observance, in Auchindoun in the middle of the Bone Wastes. Dealer Tariq, a Shady Dealer, sells goods here. Provisioner Tsaalt says fighting is underway inside Auchindoun and his compatriots need help. Auchenai death-speakers, a Cabal spell-weaver and Levixus roam the ring.

You are in Auchenai Grounds, a battlefield in the Bone Wastes of Terokkar Forest. Commander Ra'vaj has the Auchenai and Sha'tar dead burned so their bodies cannot be used in Auchenai rituals. Auchenai initiates and doomsayers roam it, and Unliving Guardians patrol the Bone Wastes.

You are in Allerian Post, an Alliance post in Terokkar Forest. Theloria Shadecloak, an exiled high elf, works to contain the fel orc buildup nearby. Lieutenant Meridian is sure Firewing Point is building a mana bomb, and wants to strike the enemies around Allerian Stronghold.

You are in Stonebreaker Camp, a Horde camp in Terokkar Forest. Sergeant Chawni directs attacks on Firewing Point and wants its mana bomb set off to protect Stonebreaker Hold. Shadowstalker Kaide watches the fel orcs near the hold.

You are in Wayne's Refuge, a forge in Terokkar Forest where David Wayne, a human smith, works. He left the Sons of Lothar after joining the Draenor expedition, and he is remaking an anti-demon sword here.

You are in The Shadow Stair, a place in Terokkar Forest. The Consortium's laborers and engineers work here, and Artificer Morphalius and Nexus-Prince Haramad have crews stalled at the Mana-Tombs behind Nexus-Prince Shaffar's ward. Cabal skirmishers and spell-weavers haunt the stair, and a vendor called Slim deals in goods.

You are in Sha'tari Base Camp, a camp in the Bone Wastes of Terokkar Forest. Explorers' League digs are run from here by Dwarfowitz, who sends researchers out to study the creatures of the Bone Wastes. Commander Ra'vaj is strained by losses to the Auchenai, who are trying to seize the dead, and Netherweb Ridge spiders have carried off Sha'tar warriors. The camp has a first aid trainer and a blacksmithing supplier.
You are in Sorrow Wing Point, a place in Terokkar Forest. Lost Torranche are the danger here, and a number of them are about.

You are in Blackwind Landing, a Skyguard post in Terokkar Forest, just outside Skettis. Sky Sergeant Doryn sends recruits against the arakkoa from here, and Skyguard Handler Deesak runs the nether ray flights, which are strained by frequent sorties and short feed. Sky Commander Adaris is seriously wounded and under the care of the medic Severin. A quartermaster, Grella, supplies and repairs the Skyguard's equipment.

You are in Veil Harr'ik, a part of Skettis in Terokkar Forest. Time-Lost Skettis high priests, reavers and worshippers are found here, and wild kaliri birds swoop at anyone who attacks them. Skettis wing guards, windwalkers and time-shifters are dangers, along with monstrous kaliri and blackwind sabercats.

You are in Terokk's Rest, a place in Terokkar Forest where the scribe Sahaak keeps apart from the fighting. He is an old, nearly blind arakkoa and offers exotic texts for sale. Skettis wing guards, windwalkers and surgers haunt the area, and monstrous kaliri are a danger here too.

You are in Veil Ala'rak, a part of Skettis in Terokkar Forest, near Blackwind Lake. Talonpriest Ishaal, Talonpriest Skizzik and Talonpriest Zellek are part of the Skettis chain of command, and this is where they have been sought out. Skettis soulcallers, eviscerators and wing guards make the area dangerous.

You are in Upper Veil Shil'ak, a part of Skettis in Terokkar Forest. Time-Lost Skettis high priests, reavers and worshippers are found here, along with wild kaliri. Skettis sentinels and time-shifters are the dangers, along with windwalkers.
